The CELSIUS On-the-Go Powder Stick Packs in Berry flavor (Zero Sugar, 14 Sticks per Pack, 2.5 Ounce per Pack) have received a lot of positive attention for their convenience, refreshing taste, and effective energy-boosting properties. Here’s a breakdown of what customers typically highlight in their reviews:### **Taste:**Many users enjoy the **Berry flavor** of these powder sticks. It's described as **refreshing** and not overly sweet, despite being sugar-free. It strikes a balance between tart and sweet, providing a pleasant experience when mixed with water.### **Convenience:**The **on-the-go powder sticks** are frequently praised for their portability. They come in individual packets, making them incredibly convenient for people who are always on the move. Simply add one packet to water and enjoy a quick energy boost without needing to carry bulky cans or bottles.### **Performance:**CELSIUS powder sticks are marketed as a product that provides **natural energy** without the sugar crash associated with many energy drinks. The formula includes ingredients like **green tea extract, caffeine, and ginger**, which provide a clean boost of energy. Reviewers often mention feeling energized and alert after drinking, with many appreciating the **lack of jitters** or crashes.### **Zero Sugar:**For those who are watching their sugar intake, the zero-sugar aspect is a significant selling point. Customers often note that they can enjoy a flavorful energy drink without the negative effects of sugar, like an insulin spike or crash.### **Health Focus:**CELSIUS is positioned as a **fitness and wellness product**, so it's marketed as being free from artificial preservatives, flavors, and sweeteners. Many reviews highlight the product’s **health-conscious ingredients**, which include **vitamins and minerals** that may support metabolism.### **Drawbacks:**Some customers mention that the flavor can be a bit **strong or artificial** for certain tastes, especially if mixed with too little water. Also, while the caffeine boost works for many, those sensitive to caffeine might find it a bit too strong.### **Packaging:**The compact, lightweight packaging makes it perfect for tossing in a gym bag or backpack. The 14-stick pack provides a decent quantity for frequent use, though some users might find it runs out quickly if consumed regularly.Overall, **CELSIUS On-the-Go Powder Stick Packs** are highly rated for their **convenience**, **taste**, and **energy-boosting effects**. They're an excellent option for individuals looking for a sugar-free, healthy alternative to traditional energy drinks. If you enjoy berry-flavored drinks and need a quick pick-me-up, this product is likely a good fit. Just be mindful of the caffeine content if you're sensitive to stimulants.

As wrestler, I am very concerned with diet, exercise, and getting as much long lasting energy as possible from everything that I eat (yes believe it or not most successful wrestlers do eat. They just know what to eat and when)! Spark is something I live on both in and out of my season! Long lasting energy, no crash, and compared to most energy supplements extremely healthy!! But that's only half the battle. The other half is finding something that tastes good enough that you are actually excited to take it, and spark does just that! Three scoops (which are surprisingly small) of this stuff spread out throughout the day has been enough to get me through grueling tournaments (including my time at the Colorado state tournament) with ease. Personally I mix a scoop of this with a scoop of Accelerade to make the ultimate energy/recovery/rehydration drink I have ever had. And the best part about spark is that it triples as both a preworkout, energy supplement during your workout, or postworkout/rehydration suppliment depending on when you take it.Outside of wrestling, I am a lifter, work at a tire shop, and particpate in many other sports and community service projects. Through it all, Spark is my go to choice for energy when I need it. Not soda, not red bull, not gatoraid, and not other types of quick energy replacement suppliments. Although I am sure these things do work for other people, I have found that Spark is not only the healthiest of these options, but (at least for me) also one of the most effective options as well. Even on those weigh in days for wrestling or just a normal day when no water is available, I love the taste enough to be able to just put the powder straight in my mouth and take it that way.In terms of the actual product, it mixes very well. Minimal clumping even when it might be a little more saturated than normal due to the lack of enough water and it mixes well with other products (such as Accelerade) nicely if you like to do that. Out of the many flavors I prefer the fruit punch the best, however I have tried all the flavors and would not hesitate to buy any of them if the fruit punch was sold out. You do have to rinse your water bottle a few times to get it all out after you drink it but that is pretty typical of any type of supplement or energy drink. If you have never tried Spark before, I know it might look a little pricey, but it is worth the money! I would definitely recommend trying it out! Take it from the wrestler and just an everyday person who has tried just about everything when it comes to energy/rehydration suppliments out there.

This stuff is pretty great! I've typically been drinking a can each morning before my run and I have burned more calories from the energy it gives me than I was burning previous to drinking these. That's definitely what they mean by "burn an extra 100 calories". Simply drinking Celsius will not shed any pounds; it is meant to be a supplement to aid in calorie burning.Although Celsius seems to be an excellent source of energy, I learned the hard way not to drink it at night. I was so excited to receive them that as soon as they arrived at 7pm, I immediately chugged an entire can. While my run was awesome and filled with energy that night, I finished the run and spotlessly cleaned every surface in my apartment, vaccumed every inch of carpet, scrubbed all of my tile, and pointlessly did laundry and other various chores that were definitely not necessary. Having all of that energy was great until it was suddenly 3am and I was unable to fall asleep to wake up at 6am for work! Big mistake.The flavors aren't too bad, either:Raspberry Acai Green Tea - This one is, by far, my favorite. Perhaps it's just because I love tea, but the flavor is nice and refreshing. It almost tastes like a low calorie snapple.Sparkling Orange - While I'm not a fan of carbonation, this flavor wasn't bad at all. To me, it tasted like diet orange soda.Sparkling Wild Berry - Another carbonated flavor that isn't too bad if you like that kind of thing. I thought it tasted like a fruity soda.Cola - This tastes EXACTLY like diet Pepsi.Green Tea Peach Mango - This flavor was also quite good. You can definitely taste the fruit in it, which is comforting and yummy.So basically, if you're looking to boost the energy in your workouts, I would suggest Celsius. It's a million times better than any other energy drink on the market and it's much better for your health. Try it out!

I bought this as a temporarily replacement to Monster as a caffeine source since I couldn't get to a store to buy a pack, and I was pleasantly surprised. First off, please note that I paid only $11 for these since I had a gift card to apply, so I'm not so sure if I'd find it worth the $20 price tag in the future. I usually have to drink a full energy drink to get through any day, and I can barely feel the caffeine's effects when I drink one. With these, I could feel energized (I believe that's because there's a little more caffeine in a can of this than there is in a Monster); it did make me a little jittery, so if you don't like that feeling, these might not be for you. I personally don't regularly work out, but my friend does, so I gave him a few of the cans to try, and he found that he enjoyed his workout more those days. For me, the fact that they're all 5 or 10 calories is good enough since I don't work out. As for the flavors, there are five different ones, and my friend and I enjoyed each one except for the cola, but hey, I can overlook one bad flavor for all the caffeine these have.

I suffer from chronic fatigue syndrome and have to take medication daily to help combat it, but it still doesn't work completely. Getting going in the morning, staying focused, energized, and physically motivated has been a struggle for me since childhood, and genetically I metabolize caffeine at much faster rate than what is considered to be average or normal (I had DNA genome testing done). This means the amount of caffeine I need to consume in order to benefit from its effects is much greater, and the duration of its effects is considerably shorter. I end up having to drink caffeinated beverages all day long just to stay awake, but it does very little in regards to keeping me from feeling sleepy or physically exhausted. Unfortunately this has also led to weight gain because I'm not as active as I'd like to be.I've tried every energy drink, every caffeinated gum, every powder, every energy pill. They either don't work well enough, are too sweet, make me feel nauseous or shaky rather than energized, cause headaches or sugar crashes and leave me feeling worse.I ordered a case of Celsius not knowing what to expect, but willing to give it a go. The fact that it is sugar free, aspartame free, free of artificial preservatives, high fructose corn syrup, and free from artificial coloring and flavors was the high selling point for me. The burning an extra 100 calories claim was just a bonus, but also intriguing. I hoped that it wouldn't taste awful. I'm very happy to say that not only does it work at keeping me energized and not just awake, it tastes great!My favorite are the two non-carbonated flavors, but the carbonated flavors aren't horrible though, even the cola which I was dubious about.Just ONE of these in the morning has completely replaced my need to drink copious amounts of coffee, tea, or soda throughout the day. Only one day did I have Celsius and coffee both. It makes me feel awake, focused, and most of all I get things DONE! It doesn't make me feel nauseous, shaky, give me headaches or cause any kind of crash either!I'm am SO glad I tried this! This is a total game changer for me! I am now completely out and ordered another case.Word of advice: if you drink it too late in the day you're gonna be up all night. The first time I tried it I drank it at around 7pm because I was falling asleep and needed to cook dinner. I ended up not being able to sleep until about 4 am. Also, if you're sensitive to caffeine I'd drink half and wait to see how it affects you before drinking the other half. My friend tried one when visiting because I was raving about it and it made him really shaky and anxious before he even finished it.I'm a complete convert and now I don't think I could go a day without having one in the morning.Highly recommend trying! Not only does it work, it's not full of nasty chemicals. Who could ask for anything more?**Update 12/6/16**I still drink one of these a day, sometimes two depending on what I'm doing and how much energy I need. I basically only drink the Cola and the Raspberry Acai flavors at this point.I tried the Watermelon recently and I don't like it at all. It has that chemical watermelon taste to it that watermelon gum has. Gah! I don't recommend that one. It's the ONLY flavor I've tried that I flat out dislike. It's way too sweet. I still have the case in my pantry. If I'm out of my regular flavors I will down one quickly before it loses any of its coldness. It's honestly the only way a I can get it down, bleh!Avoid!Despite the nastiness of the Watermelon, Celsius is still part of my daily routine. It's still the only drink to have the effects I'm looking for in an energy drink.I've even gotten a friend hooked and she now orders them and drinks them daily as well.My mom has MS and has a lot of lethargy because of it. She was drinking a few of the leading brands of energy drinks, and all the chemicals in them worried me, especially with how much of them she was drinking. I recommended that she try out Celsius, and now she drinks one a day and no longer needs to drink the other brands, and she is able to function much better all around. She swears by them and tells me she isn't getting headaches anymore, doesn't get jittery and her stamina for physical activity has improved greatly.

I personally am a connoisseur of energy drinks. I rely on caffeine for most of my projects at school and for late night coding sessions as well as marathon gaming. Although energy drinks can be considered a crutch, it's a lifestyle decision that many, many people embrace rather than attempt to avoid... I am one of these people.That said, Guru Energy is fairly cheap ($1.25USD/can) if you buy it here off Amazon, it comes in the Redbull standard 8.3 fl/oz cans, and is shipped in a suprisingly lightweight and compact case (compare this to Monster, Rockstar, or any other brand with standard 16 fl/oz cans).The taste, like Guru's website describes, is very indescribable. It is very sharp and light with a medium amount of carbonation. The caffeine buzz is more "natural"... it has more of an upslope and downslope rather than a sudden cracked out (which is arguably awesome too in its own respect) then big crash sort of feeling. This is because the caffeine in Guru is derived from 125mg of Guaranine (Guarana Herb) rather than synthetically separated then added. There is no mention about how much of the 125mg of Guaranine is real caffeine, but since Red Bull checks in at 80mg / 8.3oz it seems that Guru is in pretty good shape.I think a particular good feature of Guru is that it uses cane sugar rather than high fructose corn syrup. I appriciate a good quality soda, particularly microbrew colas, and they often exclusively contain cane sugar.So in summary, this energy drink is farily cheap, good buzz, all natural, and great for coding, gaming, or studying.

Sadly, the replacement drinks were the same new "cane syrup" formula that tastes terrible. The art on the can is different than what Amazon shows in the listing. And the ingredients list shown in the Amazon listing still states cane sugar. This is false advertising. ***Please change the drink back to the original formula*** Or at least stop false advertising.

One tasted like Original and one tasted Lite despite both being Original cans. Come to find out after some online sleuthing - THERE'S BEEN A RECIPE CHANGE! They've replaced organic cane SUGAR with SYRUP and its ruined the taste completely. I wish they had advertised this prior to my latest purchase (which will be my last) that was unable to be returned. It was a good run Guru, but you've lost a loyal customer. This one hurts just as bad as when RedBull discontinued their cranberry flavor :(

What can I say about Celsius Essentials Dragonberry, other than it's quite possibly the most delicious energy drink you will ever have in your entire life? When it comes to Celsius, this is hands down the best flavor out of *all* of them, the slender can flavors included. All others are inferior, and once you taste the sweet, refreshing flavor of strawberries mixed with the light, airy taste of pitaya (dragonfruit for the layman), you will never want another. Grape? Think again. That nasty orange marshmallow one? Ugh, no thank you. Cherry Lime? Not this time. Blue Razz? Get out of here with that azz. Watermelon? Well... I mean okay maybe you can drink this one, because *I* will drink this one... but only if there's no Dragonberry available! But seriously, this is great. It's such a great flavor that everyone loves it, and the gas station across the street from my home attempts to keep them in stock for me, as I will purchase 3-4 cans at a time several times a week. But they sell out so fast that I can only get them from there for the first few days after they restock all their Celsius flavors, because everyone else buys the Dragonberry ones, too, so very shortly the gas station has a cooler with one empty slot for a line of cans of Dragonberry Celsius, and then a bunch of slots full of every other color. Grape and Watermelon sell out next, and nobody likes that gross orange one that tastes like perfume, so they really should just discontinue it and come up with something actually good to take its place. But until then, just do yourself a favor and drink the Dragonberry.This thing has a good amount of carbonation, enough to tickle your nose and maybe make you have one or two of those little tiny burps but you're not going to go around belching like a dragon after drinking it like SOME energy drinks can do to you. With 300mg of caffeine, they recommend you limit yourself to two of these a day, but I often have two of these Celsius plus 3-4 cups of coffee in the morning and haven't had any adverse effects, though this is coming from someone with very high caffeine tolerance. As I also suffer from ADHD, I don't really get an energy burst from these drinks, but they *do* help me focus and can sometimes take the edge off of some of my ADHD symptoms  in a much more efficient manner than coffee. I've also never had a stomach ache or bloating after drinking Celsius, even if I dare to have three in one day, which I can't say for some other energy drinks that claim to do stuff like give you wings.Liars.But you know what? The makers of Celsius don't lie. Their product is good, contains ingredients you don't have to be afraid of, and has studies backing up their claims regarding the effects of Celsius on your metabolism while exercising. If you want an energy drink you can trust and that tastes great instead of like battery acid, Dragonberry Celsius is for you.It's definitely for me.

Monster’s Viking Berry flavor is a bold addition to their energy drink lineup, and it definitely makes a statement. It’s sweet but not overwhelmingly so, with a slight tartness that keeps it from being syrupy. There’s also a faint herbal undertone, which gives it a slightly different edge than your typical fruit-based energy drinks. If you like berry flavors with a little attitude, this one delivers.Energy Boost:Like most Monsters, it’s packed with caffeine, taurine, B-vitamins, and all the usual suspects. I felt the boost within about 15–20 minutes, and it kept me going for a solid few hours without the jittery crash. It’s ideal for a mid-afternoon slump or before a workout.Design & Vibe:The can design is eye-catching—dark, with Nordic-inspired artwork that totally leans into the “Viking” theme. It looks cool and stands out on the shelf, which is always a plus.Downsides:It is high in sugar so if you're sensitive to that or prefer more subtle flavors, it might be a bit much. Also, like with most energy drinks, it’s not something I’d recommend drinking daily due to the high caffeine and sugar content (unless you're getting the sugar-free version, if available).Bottom Line:Viking Berry is a solid, flavorful option for energy drink fans who want something fruity but not basic. It’s got the classic Monster energy punch wrapped in a bold berry flavor with a unique twist. Definitely worth trying at least once—especially if you're into themed, collectible cans.

The Bad Apple Monster is an outstanding example of how a simple, familiar idea can be transformed into something creative, meaningful, and memorable. By taking the well-known phrase “one bad apple spoils the bunch” and turning it into a literal monster, the concept immediately resonates with audiences. It feels clever without being confusing, and imaginative without being overcomplicated. From the moment you encounter the Bad Apple Monster, it’s clear that this is not just another generic creature, but a thoughtfully designed symbol with depth and personality.One of the strongest aspects of the Bad Apple Monster is its visual design. Apples are usually associated with health, sweetness, and simplicity, so seeing one twisted into something monstrous instantly creates a sense of unease. The contrast between the familiar and the corrupted is what makes the monster so effective. Whether the apple appears bruised, rotten, cracked open, or dripping with decay, every visual detail reinforces the idea that something once good has gone wrong. This visual storytelling makes the monster easy to recognize and hard to forget.Beyond its appearance, the Bad Apple Monster succeeds because of what it represents. It works on a symbolic level, suggesting how negativity, corruption, or bad behavior can spread and influence others. This makes the monster feel relevant and relatable rather than random. It can represent a toxic person in a group, a harmful idea, or even a personal flaw that grows if left unchecked. Because of this, the Bad Apple Monster can be interpreted in many different ways depending on the context, which adds to its strength as a concept.The Bad Apple Monster is also versatile. It can function effectively as a villain in a story, a cautionary figure in a lesson, or a creative character in artwork or games. In a narrative, it could be the source of corruption, slowly infecting everything around it. In an educational or moral context, it could serve as a visual reminder of the importance of accountability and positive influence. This flexibility makes it more valuable than a monster that exists purely to scare.Another impressive quality of the Bad Apple Monster is how it balances being unsettling with being engaging. While its rotten or corrupted features may be disturbing, there is also something oddly fascinating about it. This balance keeps it from becoming overwhelming or off-putting. Instead, it draws people in, encouraging them to look closer and think more deeply about what the monster represents. This is a difficult balance to achieve, and the Bad Apple Monster handles it well.Creativity is at the heart of this concept. Monsters often rely on extreme size, violence, or complexity to stand out, but the Bad Apple Monster proves that originality matters more. By grounding the monster in a familiar object and then subverting expectations, it achieves impact through clever design rather than excess. This makes it accessible to a wide audience while still feeling unique.Overall, the Bad Apple Monster is a highly effective and well-executed concept. Its strong symbolism, striking design, and versatility set it apart from more generic monsters. It leaves a lasting impression not just because of how it looks, but because of what it represents. The Bad Apple Monster is proof that powerful ideas don’t need to be complicated—they just need to be thoughtful, creative, and well realized.
